clue.text: Contract killer's abandoned student son Charlie

indicators.note: abandoned means the student is left behind, dropped out of the killer's name

parts.note: the Jackal is the hired assassin of Frederick Forsyth's novel The Day of the Jackal, so 'Contract killer's' gives JACKAL'S
L is the learner, a student driver's plate
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A hitman's student son has been abandoned, apparently a family tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the L from JACKAL'S to leave JACKAS, then add S. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a fool or idiot, the same as a donkey-brained jackass.

clue.text: Smart bird picks up cracked nut

indicators.note: picks up means takes into itself, so the bird holds the other letters

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: cracked means broken open, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever bird lifts a nut that has been broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty means stylish and perky, as a smart hat worn at an angle is.

clue.text: Order tonic water from Paris infused with a dash of rough liqueur

indicators.note: infused with means a letter is steeped into the rest
order means put in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
eau is French for water

indicators.note: a dash of means just a small amount, the first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A bar order: tonic and French water with a splash of something rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads like a drinks order, but it is the instruction to rearrange tonic; 'water from Paris' is the French word, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a brand of triple sec.

clue.text: Space to include new stadium

indicators.note: to include means to hold the next letter inside

parts.note: an area is a space

explanation.surface: Room is made for a new sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or shows, much like a stadium.

clue.text: Its amazing bonding powers are not to be sniffed at!

definitions.text: Its amazing bonding powers are not to be sniffed at!

parts.words: Its amazing bonding powers are not to be sniffed at!
parts.note: an extremely strong adhesive, whose fumes are dangerous to inhale, so 'not to be sniffed at' is literal as well as the idiom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to be sniffed at' usually means impressive; here it is also a warning against glue-sniffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanoacrylate adhesive that sets almost instantly with remarkable strength.

clue.text: Fine gold cross foolish person returned in blunder

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: returned means the fool's word is sent back the other way

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Wearing a gold cross with a fine chain, an idiot came back having made a social gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A faux pas is a social gaffe, literally a 'false step' in French.

clue.text: Return of peculiar area for discussion

indicators.note: return means the little word of is turned back

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A strange area set aside for debate comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a place or meeting where ideas and views are exchanged.

clue.text: Forced Alan out with U-turn

indicators.note: out means put out of order, the letters scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters UTURN

explanation.surface: Alan has been forced out of office by a policy U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural behaviour is strained or affected, as forced laughter is.

clue.text: More natural, happy noise from cat after eating sardine's tail

indicators.note: after eating means the cat's noise takes in the next letter

parts.note: a contented cat purrs

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of the fish's name

parts.note: the fish whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: The cat purrs happily after eating a sardine.
explanation.definitionFit: Purer means less adulterated or mixed, closer to its unprocessed state.

clue.text: Team reportedly considers moving laterally

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so a word that sounds like weighs

parts.note: weighs means considers, as in weighs up

explanation.surface: A team is said to be thinking about a sideways transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going sideways means travelling to the side rather than forwards, crabwise.

clue.text: Join backing for Brussels saving money

indicators.note: backing for means the whole lot is read back to front
saving means holding, so the money sits inside Brussels' letters

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: An appeal to join in support of the European project while keeping money safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for cash; the reversal applies to the whole container, not just Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things is to bring them together as one, to merge or combine them.

clue.text: Married Dad embarrassed to admit pretence periodically

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for dad
red-faced, so red

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of pretence is used

parts.note: the word from which every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Dad, newly wed, is red-faced at confessing a little play-acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' takes R, T, N, E from pretence; PA + RED takes them in.
explanation.definitionFit: To have partnered someone is to have paired up with them, as a spouse does in a wedding.

clue.text: When retired, Mrs Thatcher acquired 15 finally (a four-letter word)

indicators.note: acquired means took in, so a letter is placed inside the reversed name
retired means withdrawn, going back, so her first name runs backwards

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, the former UK prime minister

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of that answer

parts.note: the answer to 15 down

explanation.surface: Retired, Mrs Thatcher picked up a nickname, and a rude short word.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' points to the answer of 15 down, whose last letter is wanted. 'Four-letter word' sounds like a swear word but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, from Greek tetra-, four, and gramma, letter.

clue.text: Chuck topless bird out of London airport

indicators.note: out of means the remaining letters are taken away from the airport's name

parts.note: Heathrow is London's main airport

indicators.note: topless means the bird loses its first letter

parts.note: the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw a bird without its head out of Heathrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' turns RHEA into HEA, which comes out of HEATHROW.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is to toss or hurl it, an informal way of saying fling.

clue.text: Theatre work which hardly leaves 'em in stitches

definitions.text: Theatre work which hardly leaves 'em in stitches

parts.words: Theatre work which hardly leaves 'em in stitches
parts.note: the operating theatre, not the stage: minimally invasive surgery through tiny cuts needs hardly any stitches, rather than a comedy leaving audiences laughing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' and 'in stitches' suggest a comedy show; it is the hospital operating theatre and surgical sutures.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimally invasive surgery done through small incisions using cameras and instruments, so patients need few sutures.

clue.text: Shower with Rolling Stones?

parts.note: a downpour of ice pellets, called hailstones, tumbling from the sky, not a gig by the rock band

explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised Rolling Stones suggests the rock band; the stones are lumps of ice rolling along after falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in which pellets of ice fall instead of rain, sometimes the size of pebbles.

clue.text: Rob's quite horrible nickname

indicators.note: horrible means the letters are made a mess of

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rob has been given a rather horrible nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is an informal epithet or byname given to a person.

clue.text: Formerly poorest island, according to Spooner

indicators.note: named after Rev Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: worst means poorest in quality
an isle is an island

explanation.surface: The island was once the poorest of all, Spooner tells us.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'worst isle' and move the W sound across: 'erst' and 'while'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an old-fashioned adverb for at one time or previously.

clue.text: Penultimate part of drama is tense — one stands up

parts.note: a classic play has five acts, so the second last is act four, ACT IV in Roman numerals
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: The fourth act of the play is tense, and an actor rises.
explanation.walkthrough: Five-act plays end with Act V, so the penultimate part is ACT IV.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist is a campaigner who stands up for a cause and protests.

clue.text: Vintage claret Ibis served around five for you or me?

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or wine of a recognised quality, a vintage

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap round the five
served as in dished up, a reworking of the letters

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A vintage claret is served to an Ibis, perhaps a restaurant, around five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'you or me' as the person doing this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruciverbalist is a crossword solver or setter, as the reader and the setter both are.

clue.text: Silvery mineral on the beach

parts.note: ash is a silvery-grey shade, as in ash-blonde
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A shiny silver mineral is found on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, having come out of the water onto the shore.

clue.text: River Island stocking new designer underwear tops

indicators.note: stocking means holding as stock, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: IS is the map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: tops means the top, first letters of each word

parts.note: the two words whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: River Island, the British high-street fashion chain, stocks new designer underwear tops.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a UK clothing retailer, so 'River' looks like part of the store name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Asia, flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Most senior editor upset regimental HQ

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so read from the bottom up in a down clue

parts.note: top means most senior

explanation.surface: The editor-in-chief has upset the army's headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military base where a regiment keeps stores and recruits.

clue.text: Onset of terrible season leaving, er, snow blowing around friendly communities

indicators.note: onset of means the beginning, so just the first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

indicators.note: leaving means the er goes out of winter

parts.note: winter is a season
taken as written

indicators.note: blowing around suggests the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: As a terrible winter begins, er, snow is blowing around.
explanation.walkthrough: WINTER without ER leaves WINT; snow rearranged gives OWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin towns are places in different countries paired for cultural exchange and goodwill.

clue.text: Subject right out of line in Geography lesson?

indicators.note: out of means the right is removed from the line

parts.note: a tropic is a line of latitude met in geography

explanation.surface: A schoolchild asks what subject the geography lesson's line is.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Component of softer rare earth

indicators.note: Component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part of some softer rare earth element, in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for land or ground, used in English as in terra firma.

clue.text: Spontaneous, Julius is ready for delivery. You?

parts.note: Julius is the setter, so 'Julius is' is I'm from the setter's point of view
prompt means quick and on time, ready to deliver
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: The setter declares being ready to hand over the goods, and asks if the solver is.
explanation.walkthrough: Julius is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Julius is' stands for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without preparation or rehearsal, on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Horny beast Greek character beds at home

indicators.note: beds means takes in, so a word goes inside the Greek letter

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
in means at home

explanation.surface: A lustful Greek takes lovers to bed at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' in its literal sense of having a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is the beast famous for the horn on its snout.

clue.text: Carry Head of Military in command, of symbolic importance

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: The army's leader carries a symbol of high importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something totemic is emblematic, serving as a symbol like a totem pole.

clue.text: Swingers bar?

parts.note: not a nightclub for partner-swapping but the bar that circus acrobats swing on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub for swingers; it is the acrobats' apparatus.
